## Further Reading

Datar, S. M., & Rajan, M. V. (2021). *Horngren's cost accounting: A managerial emphasis* (17th ed.). Pearson. <https://www.pearson.com/en-us/pearsonplus/p/9780136713845> Its chapter on flexible budgets and direct-cost variances explains the direct labor efficiency variance, which compares the direct labor hours actually used with the hours allowed for the output produced, and its chapter on overhead variances explains where indirect costs appear. The direct part of this chapter's monthly measure is the quantity behind the first variance, and the indirect part belongs to the second.

Hyndman, R. J., & Athanasopoulos, G. (2021). *Forecasting: Principles and practice* (3rd ed.). OTexts. <https://otexts.com/fpp3/> A free online textbook on forecasting. Its section on moving averages (3.3) explains how an average over several periods smooths out short-term swings, although it centers its averages where a management report uses trailing ones, and its section on differencing (9.1) explains why comparing a month with the same month of the previous year removes a seasonal pattern.

Kimball, R., & Ross, M. (2013). *The data warehouse toolkit: The definitive guide to dimensional modeling* (3rd ed.). Wiley. The standard guide to organizing data for reporting and analysis. Its treatment of facts recorded at a chosen grain, such as a month, and of summaries built on top of them, is the background to building measures like the one in this chapter as repeatable objects rather than one-off queries.

Loraas, T. M., & Searcy, D. L. (2010). Using queries to automate journal entry tests: Agile Machinery Group, Inc. *Issues in Accounting Education*, *25*(1), 155–174. <https://doi.org/10.2308/iace.2010.25.1.155> In this case, students act as an outsourced internal audit team and query nearly a million journal entry records of a real company. They compare the entries each module should produce with the entries actually made, and isolate entries for further study. It extends the journal entry tests of Exercise 11.5.

Molinaro, A., & de Graaf, R. (2020). *SQL cookbook: Query solutions and techniques for all SQL users* (2nd ed.). O'Reilly Media. A collection of solutions to common query problems, written for Oracle, DB2, SQL Server, MySQL, and PostgreSQL rather than SQLite. Its chapters on window functions, date arithmetic, and reporting show many variations on the techniques of this chapter, such as running totals, rankings, and pivoted reports, and translating them to SQLite is good practice.

Pencavel, J. (2015). The productivity of working hours. *The Economic Journal*, *125*(589), 2052–2076. <https://doi.org/10.1111/ecoj.12166> A study of the output and working hours of munition workers, most of them women. Below a threshold of hours, output rose in proportion to hours; above it, each additional hour added less output. It is useful background for reading a rising overtime share, because hours beyond the threshold may buy less output than the hours before them.
